# 1 Clement Chapter 22 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 22 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_022_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 22

**22:1** Now faith in Christ confirms all these things; for he himself through the Holy Spirit calls us thus: "Come, children, hearken to me; I will teach you the fear of the Lord."

**22:2** "Who is the man that desires life, that loves to see good days?

**22:3** Keep your tongue from evil, and your lips from speaking guile.

**22:4** Turn away from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it.

**22:5** The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and his ears toward their cry for help.

**22:6** But the face of the Lord is against those who do evil, to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth." [Ps 34:11-16 LXX]

**22:7** And again: "The righteous man cried, and the Lord hearkened to him, and delivered him from all his troubles." [Ps 34:17 LXX]

**22:8** "Many are the troubles of the righteous man, but the Lord will deliver him from them all." [Ps 34:19 LXX]

**22:9** "Many are the troubles of the sinner, but mercy will surround him who hopes in the Lord." [Ps 32:10 LXX]

---

*EMET: Christ himself is the speaker of Psalm 34 (v.1, "he himself through the Holy Spirit calls us") — a striking christological reading. Clement presents the Psalm as the voice of Christ addressing the Corinthians. This is a christological interpretation of the Psalter.*
